item.title: Recommendations for Regulators
item.lead: The policy direction from the dossier can be translated into a practical supervisory agenda without priorly establishing the source claims as proven.

blocks.text: For regulators, a primary priority lies with transparency regarding identity and automation. Investigation can commence with the question of what information a consumer actually receives about who is communicating and which components are supported by systems.

A second priority is data governance. Regulators can examine which categories of personal information are stored in CRM systems, who has access, how long information is retained, and which data are commercially utilized.

A third priority is supply chain responsibility. Not only the front-end platform, but also the agency, payment processor, and operational service provider can be included in an audit. The dossier specifically emphasizes the risks of fragmentation.

A fourth priority is pattern analysis of microtransactions. Not every small amount is suspicious, but cumulative patterns, unusual payouts, and unclear counterparties can provide grounds for further investigation within existing compliance and fraud frameworks.
